gen-dafont-joystix-gf-noto-sans-zanabaza: Approachable and tall in the x-height, Noto Sans Zanabazar Square keeps its wide gaps crisp even at tiny sizes. Joystix adds the arcade punch above it.

gen-dafont-joystix-gf-numans: Chunky, stamped, and a bit rowdy: Joystix has the restrained thick-thin play of a worn wooden stamp. Numans does the opposite job, with a sans-serif that tucks tightly coiled lowercase into generous tracking.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-onest: Approachable is the word for this duo, with Joystix's arcade swagger leading and its understated stroke variation. Onest follows in a plain sans of short ascenders and big bowls, drawn at a wire-like thickness that glides along over many lines.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-open-sans: Open Sans brings a smooth, unclogged read in bulky lowercase proportions, a plain sans with no fuss. Joystix sits above it with mid-level stroke contrast and arcade attitude, and Open Sans lets it be the loud one.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-orienta: Joystix leads with arcade boldness, its bowls thinning gracefully but never sharply across widely tracked letters. Orienta follows in sans-serif, its counters breathing like a hollow reed, and the quiet gap between cases is the strongest thing about it.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-oxygen: Joystix stamps out its arcade letters with medium-low contrast and a compact gap up to the ascenders. And Oxygen, a plain sans with curves that never close back on themselves, can take a modest size.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-parkinsans: Joystix brings a bold, arcade look with a gentle thick-thin rhythm in widely tracked letters. But Parkinsans does the crisp work, a sans whose single stroke thickness stays followable even when shrunk.
